song_story.overview: Lion Heart is the title track off Girls' Generation's 2015 album of the same name, released after several members had already been in the group for eight years. The song is a retro, brass-heavy dance track built around a hunting metaphor — the singer compares her love interest to a lion who keeps circling, sizing up prey, never quite committing. She's done chasing. Now she wants to be the one who tames him. It's playful rather than heartbroken, more confident flirtation than longing.
song_story.cultural_root: The song leans on 길들이다 (gildeurida) — to tame or domesticate — which carries a specific flavor in Korean pop culture: the idea of taming a wild, emotionally unavailable partner rather than changing yourself to chase them. It flips the usual K-pop pining trope. Instead of begging someone to notice her, the singer positions herself as the one in control, deciding she's the one who gets to do the taming. That confident, slightly teasing tone was part of Girls' Generation reinventing themselves as more mature performers years into their career.

verse_1.lines: Ooh, 너와 너 처음 만났을때 / Ooh, 마치 사자처럼 맴돌아 / 기회를 노려 / 내 맘 빼신 너 / Ah, 넌 달라진 게 없어 여전히 / 난 애가 타고 또 타 / 사냥감 찾아 / 한 눈 파는 너 / 수백 번 밀어내야 했는데 (Ooh-ooh-ooh-ooh) / 수천 번 널 떠나야 했는데 / 왜 맘이, 맘이 자꾸 흔들리니? / 난 여기, 여기 네 옆에 있잖니 / 정신 차려, lion heart
verse_1.literal: When you and I first met / like a lion you circled around, watching for a chance / you stole my heart / you're still the same, unchanged / I keep burning with impatience / searching for prey, your eyes wandering elsewhere
verse_1.context: The whole verse sets up an extended metaphor: he's a lion sizing up prey (사냥감), and she's the one getting swept in emotionally while he keeps scanning for something else. 애가 타다 is a set phrase meaning to be anxious or burn with worry — literally 'my insides scorch.' It's used constantly in Korean for romantic frustration.

pre_chorus.lines: 난 애가 타 / 내 맘이, 맘이 더는 식지 않게 / 난 여기저기 뛰노는 너의 맘 / 길들일래, lion heart / Ooh, 넌 자유로운 영혼 여전해 / 충실해 본능 앞에 / 지금 네 옆에 / 난 안 보이니? / 수백 번 고민고민 해봐도 (Ooh-ooh-ooh-ooh) / 수천 번 결국 답은 너인데 / 왜 맘이, 맘이 자꾸 흔들리니? / 난 여기, 여기 네 옆에 있잖니 / 정신 차려, lion heart
pre_chorus.literal: I should have pushed you away hundreds of times / I should have left you thousands of times
pre_chorus.context: 수백 번, 수천 번 — hundreds of times, thousands of times — is a common Korean intensifier pattern for exaggerating how many times you tried and failed to do something. The -아야/어야 했는데 ending means 'should have done X but didn't,' expressing regret over her own weakness for him.

chorus.lines: 난 애가 타 / 내 맘이, 맘이 더는 식지 않게 / 난 여기저기 뛰노는 너의 맘 / 길들일래, lion heart / Oh, oh, oh, oh, oh-oh, oh-oh (큰일 났어) / Oh, oh, oh, oh, oh-oh, oh-oh (큰일 났어; 곤히 잠자는 나의 코끝을, baby) / Oh, oh, oh, oh, oh-oh, oh-oh (큰일 났어, 혼 좀 나 볼래) / Oh, oh, oh, oh, oh-oh, oh-oh (네가 건드려, 나도 화가 나, baby) / 왜 맘이, 맘이 자꾸 흔들리니? (자꾸 흔들리니-리니?) / 난 여기, 여기 네 옆에 있잖니 (Woah) / 정신 차려, lion heart (Oh, 정신 차려, lion heart, yeah, yeah) / 난 애가 타 (*난 애가 타*) / 내 맘이, 맘이 더는 식지 않게 (*내 맘이, 맘이 더는 식지 않게, 않게*)
chorus.literal: Tell me why / why does my heart keep wavering? / I'm right here, right beside you / snap out of it, lion heart / I'm burning with anxiety / so my heart won't grow cold anymore / your heart that runs wild everywhere / I'm going to tame it, lion heart
chorus.context: 정신 차려 (jeongshin charyeo) is a blunt, everyday command — 'get it together' or 'snap out of it,' the kind of thing you'd say to a friend who's being careless. Here it's aimed at him, like she's scolding the lion. 길들일래 uses -(으)ㄹ래, a casual ending for stating what you intend to do, giving the line a stubborn, decided tone rather than a hopeful one.

bridge.lines: 난 여기저기 뛰노는 너의 맘 (*Ooh, 난 길들일래 lion heart*) / 길들일래, lion heart / 길들일래, lion heart / 모두 다 아니라 해도 좋을 때 있지 않아? / 사실 나만 좋음 됐지, 뭐 / 바람보다 빠른 눈치로 (맘은 뜨겁게) / 햇살처럼 따뜻한 말로 (머린 차갑게) / 길들일래 너의 lion heart / 사자 같은 너의 lion heart / Oh, oh, oh, oh, oh-oh, oh-oh (오늘부터; La, la, la, la-la, la-la-la) / 여기 와서 앉아 / Oh, oh, oh, oh, oh-oh, oh-oh (오늘부터; La, la, la, la-la, la-la-la) / 내 곁에만 있어 / Oh, oh, oh, oh, oh-oh, oh-oh (오늘부터; La, la, la, la-la, la-la-la) / 한 눈 팔지 말아
bridge.literal: Ladies, y'all know what I'm talking about, right? / Isn't there a time it's fine even if everyone else disagrees? / Honestly, it's fine as long as I'm satisfied / with instincts faster than the wind (heart heated up) / with words as warm as sunlight (mind kept cool)
bridge.context: This section breaks from singing into a half-spoken, direct-address style, talking to other women listening rather than to the love interest. 바람보다 빠른 눈치 — 'sharper instincts than the wind' — describes reading a room or a person fast. The line pairs a warm approach (따뜻한 말) with a cool head (차갑게), the tactical combination she plans to use to tame him.

artist_context: Girls' Generation released Lion Heart in 2015, roughly eight years into their career, as a deliberate shift toward a more grown, playful sound after years of cute concepts. The retro brass and swing elements were a departure meant to show range as the members moved into their late twenties, a common turning point for long-running K-pop groups.
honorific_level: informal — casual 반말 used throughout in a direct, address-to-you style

grammar_highlights.usage: Casual ending stating your own intention or preference. Appears in 길들일래 — 'I'm going to tame [him].' Gives a decided, unhesitating tone.
Expresses 'should have done X (but didn't).' Appears in 밀어내야 했는데, 떠나야 했는데 — regret over failing to walk away.
Blunt command meaning 'get it together / wake up.' Common in casual speech when scolding someone, here aimed teasingly at the love interest.
